candidates.name: Cushing's syndrome
support_spans: Serum cortisol: 1151 nmol/L (normal range: 133-537)
24-hour urine cortisol: 1375 mmol/d (normal: <275) on day 1, 1228 mmol/d on day 2
Midnight salivary cortisol: 68.6 and 59.7 nmol/L (normal: <11.3) on two consecutive nights
candidates.why: The patient's elevated cortisol levels, as indicated by multiple tests, are a hallmark of Cushing's syndrome.

candidates.name: primary parotid gland malignancy
support_spans: a mass on her left parotid gland
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy: Showed features of a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia
candidates.why: The presence of a parotid gland mass and the biopsy results indicating a salivary gland neoplasm support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: ectopic Cushing's syndrome due to parotid gland malignancy
support_spans: Immunohistochemical staining: Positive for ACTH in 30-40% of invasive tumor cells
candidates.why: The tumor's production of ACTH, as evidenced by immunohistochemical staining, suggests that the parotid gland malignancy is the cause of the patient's Cushing's syndrome.

candidates.name: Primary parotid gland malignancy
support_spans: Head, neck, and chest imaging showed a 2.4-cm parotid mass
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy: Showed features of a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia
candidates.why: The initial presentation of a parotid gland mass and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results indicating a salivary gland neoplasm with atypia support the diagnosis of a primary parotid gland malignancy.

selector.rationale: The patient's high ACTH levels and positive immunohistochemical staining for ACTH in the tumor cells, along with the development of Cushing's syndrome symptoms, support the diagnosis of an ectopic ACTH-producing tumor, which is a subtype of the broader category of Cushing's syndrome causes.

rejected.label: primary parotid gland malignancy
rejected.why: While the patient has a parotid gland malignancy, this diagnosis alone does not explain the hormonal imbalances and systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)-producing tumor
rejected.why: This is a less specific term compared to ectopic ACTH-producing tumor, given the context of the parotid gland malignancy and the ectopic production of ACTH.
